playbook:
# My Playbook for ref_estate

When I land on an unowned property early in the game (laps 1-2), I buy it. Properties generate income through rent and contribute directly to my final score, so acquiring them while I have capital is sound strategy.

When I land on an unowned property in the middle game (laps 3-4), I evaluate my cash reserves. If I have enough to purchase and still maintain a buffer of at least 50-60 in cash for unexpected rent obligations, I buy. Otherwise I pass.

When I pass START and collect salary, I add it to my balance before deciding on purchases or evaluating my position.

When I land on a property owned by another investor, I pay the rent immediately from my current cash (including any salary just received). I do not attempt to negotiate or defer.

When I land on a property I own, I declare my balance unchanged and move forward.

When I reach the final lap (lap 6), I do not buy any more properties. My score is locked into my cash plus the deed values I hold, so preserving cash at this point matters less than having deeds, but I should not spend cash that doesn't add to my final tally.

When declaring my balance, I ensure it accounts for all transfers received since my last declaration and all payments I'm making this turn.

I should have been more aggressive about buying properties early. My final score of 251 suggests I held too much cash relative to property value. Next time, buy more properties in laps 1-3 when they're available, even if it leaves me with lower cash reserves, because deed values count toward my score.
